issues.description: SealSaloon.checkOrderReady parameter mismatch: The problem statement declares a no-argument method checkOrderReady(): void in the UML (problem_statement.md line 32) and instructs orderMeal() to call that no-arg method (problem_statement.md lines 85-86). The solution implementation declares public void checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging) in src/de/tum/cit/ase/SealSaloon.java (line 20) and orderMeal() calls it with checkOrderReady(true) (src/de/tum/cit/ase/SealSaloon.java line 16). This changes the expected API (method signature) from the specification and can confuse students about which signature they must implement and how to call it.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution match the specified API by providing a no-argument public void checkOrderReady() method. Options: (A) change the solution to implement a no-arg checkOrderReady() with the specified behavior (remove the boolean parameter), or (B) add a public no-arg wrapper that delegates to the existing checkOrderReady(boolean) implementation (e.g., public void checkOrderReady() { checkOrderReady(false); }) so the signature required by the problem statement is present. Prefer (A) to keep the API identical to the specification; if internal logging is needed, implement it without changing the public signature.
